note: *pelos séculos dos séculos*: the Latinist asked five times for the singular *pelo século do século*, and the stylist for the members reversed. D27 settles the plural: it is how the phrase lives in Portuguese.
D30's headline: *orbis terræ → o mundo*. Two blind readers did not know *orbe*; the Latin psalter never has *mundus* for the world, so nothing collides. *o orbe da terra* stays selectable.
*auxílio* for *adjútor*, held against three Latinist readings (minor, then two majors asking *auxiliador*), as at 118:114 (D24, D27). HANDOFF: this row wants your ruling more than any other word.

*ao pedir contas do sangue deles*: held against two Latinist majors reading *eórum* with *recordátus est*, words he had passed twice (D27). The Latin follows the Greek, where the pronoun is the blood's. His reading is an option.
*não perecerá para sempre*: *até o fim* failed here (Latinist major, blind reader) because *até* bounds the negation. D27 keeps *in finem* its own row, not merged with *in ætérnum*.
